label: Early original-phase step (t=3-4) right after a p/u/r input that followed b/k/p, in sequences starting with e/z/o/m
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). 92% of activation mass is in the original phase, mostly at t=3 (64%) and t=4 (25%). It never fires at t=0-1 and almost never in the copy phase; a small share lands on <DEL> when L=4. It is a high-order conjunction over the short prefix. The previous input is strongly enriched for p (18x lift, 51% of mass), then u and r. The input two steps back is enriched for b, k, p. The first token is enriched for e (10x), then z, o, m. The current input matters too: v, f, 1, s, b, e push activation up. The top activations are near-exact matches of this pattern, e.g. e k p [v], e z b p [f], e k b p [<DEL>]. Adding the current-input condition gives about 0.8 precision but only about 8% recall. The chosen predicate (step 3-4, previous p/u/r, two-back b/k/p/u/r, first token e/z/o/m) reaches only about 0.29 F1 on dev and captures about 35% of activation mass. The feature looks like a specific region of hidden state set by the first few tokens, and the token sets only approximate it. It does not fire on later original positions (t>=6), on copy-phase outputs, or on sequences whose prefix lacks p/u.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=p (+5.39), orig0=e (+4.81), prev_tok=u (+3.73), prev2_tok=p (+3.69), orig0=z (+3.32), orig1=e (+3.20). Lower it: prev2_tok=e (-3.18), prev2_tok=z (-2.53), orig3=q (-1.92), L=4 & recall_idx=-1 (-1.35).
